thesis_points: Acquisition flywheel: relationship-driven bilateral sourcing → 8.16% cap rate, 18.7yr WALT, 2.2% annual bumps → 10.0% GAAP yield vs peers' 7–8%

Revenue: 77.6% service-based (car washes, medical/dental, childcare, QSR) — insulated from e-commerce disruption
$250–370M deployed per quarter at ~8% cash cap / ~10% GAAP cap regardless of implied spread noise

risks: Competitive pressure on cap rates from PE/family offices

overview.narrative:
Tower REITs dominated the tape Thursday, surging 3.47% on average with UNIT leading all names at +5.53% and CCI close behind at +3.39%, as the 10-year pulled back and investors rotated into duration-sensitive infrastructure plays ahead of tomorrow's PCE print. Office and Industrial posted solid mid-1% gains, while Hospitality flatlined at +0.03% with PEB dragging at -1.89% on continued RevPAR concerns.

The intra-sector dispersion is notable. Within Retail, UE gained 1.95% while REG shed 1.93%—nearly a 400bp spread suggesting stock-specific catalysts rather than broad thematic flows. Similarly, Healthcare saw WELL climb 2.48% against ARE's 1.32% decline, reinforcing the market's continued preference for senior housing operators over life science landlords still working through elevated vacancy. FSP's 3.43% pop in an otherwise middling Office tape warrants attention for potential positioning ahead of earnings.

Tomorrow's PCE data is the clear catalyst. Today's Tower outperformance signals the market is leaning dovish, and a soft print could extend the bid into rate-sensitive names across Net Lease and Infrastructure. We'd be cautious chasing Hospitality weakness given thin conviction either way, but would look to add Tower exposure on any post-data pullback. REG at these levels deserves a closer look if broader Retail sentiment stabilizes.
overview.narrative_short: The REIT market closed with broad strength on April 30, 2026, as all eight sectors posted gains with Tower REITs leading the advance at 3.47%. Hospitality REITs contributed modestly to the overall market rally, rising just 0.03% as the sector's relative weakness contrasted with stronger performance across other property types.
